10: `stop_point_absent` means absence of a supported point that enforces the
11: **complete required fence**, not absence of a point that can throw or stop HTTP.
12: The claim covers the shipped OpenClaw 2026.10.7 native host/provider composition
13: and supported public integration surfaces, under RelayMind's existing scope.
14: It does not claim that no arbitrary program, replacement executor, patched
15: host or later host version could implement a safe fence.

17: The frozen scope excerpts name the normative boundaries: section 1 excludes a
18: new executor; RM39 requires the native baseline and unchanged provider behavior;
19: section 7.6.1 requires current nonremoved library state as well as authority and
20: immutable bytes immediately before delivery, and preserves native ownership
21: and baseline behavior. A full replacement harness is therefore outside this
22: contract. A thin supported wrapper around the builtin attempt would still be
23: relevant; the public SDK search found no such delegation/accessor.

25: ## Why the earlier withdrawal was correct, and what changed
26: 
27: The earlier host-surface search discovered `retain()` and correctly withdrew
28: its pending negative claim. There had been no actual composition test, so the
29: candidate could not be dismissed. Its immutable inventory remains unchanged.
30: 
31: The new VPS diagnostic exercised that candidate. For positive, stale-head and
32: removed-entry sessions, genuine native ingress retained the access borrow.
33: The provider found that exact in-process borrow by session ID, and its live
34: assertion passed after the earlier RPC ended. This proves a useful retained
35: lifetime and a real provider stop point. It does not independently prove the
36: identity of the receiving turn's person.
37: 
38: At the provider boundary, the public authenticated dispatcher refused
39: `skills.library.list` with `authenticated_request_scope_unavailable`. The
40: retained borrow exposes `signal`, `assertCurrent`, and `release`; it does not
41: restore a closed authenticated request scope or supply library access. Each
42: case recorded zero receiving model requests; subsequent native retries were
43: also refused. The earlier native captures establish why a current library
44: check is necessary: removal does not prevent the host from retaining and
45: sending an immutable revision's bytes.
46: 
47: The diagnostic exited 2 because the positive loaded-byte observation was
48: intentionally stopped. Reset was `control_refused`, and revocation while
49: waiting was not run. Neither is presented as passing negative-control
50: qualification. They are not needed to demonstrate this already-missing
51: required library-currentness link; they would remain required for a positive
52: qualification.
53: 
54: ## Supported alternatives examined
55: 
56: The original hook/middleware/provider inventory and the new closure inventory
57: are complementary. Hooks and result middleware lack a live native library
58: entry capability. Public session readers expose session/pin state, which does
59: not establish a nonremoved library entry. Public skill-command and workspace
60: readers expose workspace resources, not the personal library's current entry
61: or tombstone contract. Private backing-store reads and synthesized request
62: scopes are not supported authority or currentness contracts.
63: 
64: The public custom-harness attempt carries `skillLibraryAuthoring`, so that
65: capability was not ignored. `registerAgentHarness` requires a replacement
66: `runAttempt`; its public SDK exports provide no discovered builtin-attempt
67: wrapper/getter. `runtime.agent.runEmbeddedAgent` admits another run and excludes
68: `admittedRunContext`/`preparedRunAdmission` from its public input; it is not a
69: same-attempt delegation. Implementing a new harness would be a new executor,
70: which section 1 excludes. This is a scope exclusion, not an assertion that the
71: capability is broken or every custom implementation is impossible.
72: 
73: ## Proposed disposition
74: 
75: Within that pinned supported native composition, no examined supported route
76: combines the real stop/current-authority point with the required fresh native
77: library-state check. The proposed record therefore uses `stop_point_absent`
78: and `disabled:true`. Approval requires two recorded reviews, including
79: OpenCode2, which must challenge this scope interpretation and search for any
80: missed supported **in-scope** route. A discovered route, incomplete evidence or
81: unresolved material finding prevents approval. No production registry entry is
82: added. A new host version reopens the qualification question.

owner runs every trial as operator on the owner's Apple M1 8 GiB MacBook

fixture-tested only. No gate has passed.

machine adjudicator; the owner approves by PR review). Their verifier support
is fixture-tested only.

host tasks, 20 per lane; 100 episodes) with `machine_dual.v1` labels. The
corpus is `development`, not the 300-asset acceptance catalog, so no report

paraphrase top-1 51/200 (target 0.90), control loss 0.02, resets 100/100

run-local ONNX manifest, not the preregistered one its report binds, so the
on-arm numbers are diagnostic only. The paired host run stopped after 14
tasks: the recommendations arm needs a signed-in person and disabled
skill/MCP use, 11 of 14 provider_only rows failed (`host_failed`; the cause
is not in the surviving evidence), and the run's private evidence was lost,
so it is not graded. A full two-arm host run needs about 13M external tokens. See
`docs/evidence/m10/owner-run-260/README.md`. No gate has passed.

pinned 2026.10.7 host: `m10-negative-mcp-use-openclaw-2026.10.7`
(`exact_route_absent`). No supported route invokes an independent, non-App MCP
tool by its exact native identity: `tools.invoke` is name-only, the harness
runtimes are documented private, and the App-scoped `mcp.app.callTool` does not
count. Those three verdicts rest on the pinned host source; the captures
attempted only `mcp.app.discover`, `tools.effective` and `mcp.app.listTools`

a pull request review by an org member other than the owner is written into
it, which will make MCP use a host limitation. There is **no** negative
`skill_loaded_use` record: the hooks, tool-result middleware and the provider
stream can stop a read or a request but cannot re-verify fresh person
authority, the session incarnation and the pinned bytes on their own, while
the host's `GatewaySessionAccessAuthority.retain()` borrow re-checks the
person's grant and the exact session incarnation at call time and could back a
provider `onPayload` fence. Spec 7.6.1 admits such a qualified delegation, so
`stop_point_absent` is not established; the earlier pending record asserting it
was withdrawn after review (#267). Loaded use stays disabled because it is
unqualified, not as a host limitation; its qualification attempt is #280, and
its AC30 evidence is still required on this host. Both operations stay disabled.

the first substantive captures came from CI run 41286397320. A second VPS run at

capture. Person ingress passes there. MCP use is `blocked`
(`exact_route_unqualified`). The reset case
is now `control_refused` on the real host. That run exited 2 because the
62c4dcd predicate expected one pin in the session's selection listing while
the host lists every pin of the owner profile; the selected-skill pin check

committed capture. [CI run 41340879424](https://github.com/LHCWN/relaymind/actions/runs/41340879424)
at ed21e007 completed loaded-use observation with the reset case
`control_refused`; its captures are workflow artifacts, not committed here.

probe read `payload.tools` instead of the host's `groups[].tools`; a third VPS
run at bba0cf1 with the #249 fix lists both colliding tools and is still
`blocked`, and the MCP record binds it. The MCP finding is unchanged. #259, #260 and #261 remain open and
need the real runs, captures, labels and reviews. Host configuration semantics
(#250/#240) still keep host reports below `qualified`. Spec-only decisions
awaiting implementation: the rank 4–10 choice receipt returning the offered
record, the MCP ledger location/mode/retention and erasure on reset, blind
success judging, and episode corrections through the native feedback RPC.
